sn12.44:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the origin and the passing away of the world.
sn12.44:1.3: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”
sn12.44:2.1: “And what, bhikkhus, is the origin of the world?
sn12.44:2.2: In dependence on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact.
sn12.44:2.3: With contact as condition, feeling comes to be;
sn12.44:2.8: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.44:2.9: This, bhikkhus, is the origin of the world.
sn12.44:3.1: “In dependence on the ear and sounds …
sn12.44:3.2: In dependence on the nose and odours …
sn12.44:3.3: In dependence on the tongue and tastes …
sn12.44:3.4: In dependence on the body and tactile objects …
sn12.44:3.5: In dependence on the mind and mental phenomena, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact.
sn12.44:3.6: With contact as condition, feeling comes to be; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging … existence … birth;
sn12.44:3.7: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.44:3.8: This, bhikkhus, is the origin of the world.
sn12.44:4.1: “And what, bhikkhus, is the passing away of the world?
sn12.44:4.2: In dependence on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact.
sn12.44:4.3: With contact as condition, feeling comes to be;
sn12.44:4.5: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving comes cessation of clinging;
sn12.44:4.6: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence; with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth; with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.44:4.7: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.44:4.8: This, bhikkhus, is the passing away of the world.
sn12.44:5.1: “In dependence on the ear and sounds … …
sn12.44:5.5: In dependence on the mind and mental phenomena, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact.
sn12.44:5.6: With contact as condition, feeling comes to be;
sn12.44:5.8: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving comes cessation of clinging …
sn12.44:5.9: cessation of existence … cessation of birth; with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.44:5.10: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.44:5.11: This, bhikkhus, is the passing away of the world.”
